review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read Mathlib's `AdicCompletion.pi` (`@[simps!]`), `piEquivOfFintype_apply`, and `map_of`, and the repo's test file. I found no loops. The `piEquivOfFG_symm_*` and `map_proj_piEquivOfFG_symm` lemmas look fine. The main problem is a set of overlapping simp lemmas about `piEquivOfFG`. I did not run Lean, so I can't say which rule simp tries first when several match; the claims below only say the rules overlap.

findings.excerpt:
theorem piEquivOfFG_apply (hI : I.FG) (x : AdicCompletion I (∀ j, M j)) :
    piEquivOfFG I M hI x = pi I M x :=
findings.problem: `piEquivOfFG_apply` is a simp lemma whose left side, `piEquivOfFG I M hI x`, is a subterm of the left sides of two other simp lemmas. Those are `piEquivOfFG_apply_apply` (`piEquivOfFG I M hI x j`) and `piEquivOfFG_of` (`piEquivOfFG I M hI (of I _ x)`). Simp simplifies subterms first. So on `piEquivOfFG … x j` the head `piEquivOfFG … x` can be rewritten to `pi I M x` before the whole-term lemma is tried. In that case `piEquivOfFG_apply_apply` is bypassed. The `@[simps!]`-generated lemma for `pi` presumably finishes the job there, so the lemma is redundant. For `piEquivOfFG … (of x)`, the generic lemma and `piEquivOfFG_of` both match the whole term. If the generic one wins, the result is `pi I M (of x)`, which becomes `fun j => map I (proj j) (of x)`. Mathlib's `map_of` is not a simp lemma, so that form is stuck and `piEquivOfFG_of` never fires. The file therefore has no single normal form for `piEquivOfFG`: its own proofs rewrite with `piEquivOfFG_apply` or `piEquivOfFG_apply_apply` by name, and the repo test calls `piEquivOfFG_symm_of` by name instead of using simp.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one normal form. For example, keep `piEquivOfFG_apply` as the only simp lemma that unfolds the equivalence to `pi I M`. Then make the `of` case a simp lemma for `pi I M (of I _ x)` (statement `pi I M (of I (∀ j, M j) x) = fun j => of I (M j) (x j)`). Mark `piEquivOfFG_apply_apply` and `piEquivOfFG_of` as non-simp (or delete them). Alternatively, drop the generic `piEquivOfFG_apply` from simp and keep the specific lemmas, giving `piEquivOfFG_of` and `piEquivOfFG_apply_apply` a higher priority than the generic one.
findings.benefit: Simp results for `piEquivOfFG` terms no longer depend on which overlapping rule fires first. `piEquivOfFG I M hI (of I _ x)` reliably reduces to `fun j => of I (M j) (x j)`. The unused simp lemma `piEquivOfFG_apply_apply` goes away, and users no longer have to call lemmas by name as the proofs here and the test do.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simps!]
def pi : AdicCompletion I (∀ j, M j) →ₗ[AdicCompletion I R] ∀ j, AdicCompletion I (M j) :=
theorem map_of (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (x : M) : map I f (of I M x) = of I N (f x)

theorem piEquivOfFintype_apply (x : AdicCompletion I (∀ j, M j)) :
    piEquivOfFintype I M x = pi I M x

findings.excerpt:
theorem piEquivOfFG_toLinearMap (hI : I.FG) :
    (piEquivOfFG I M hI).toLinearMap = pi I M :=
  rfl
findings.problem: `piEquivOfFG_toLinearMap` is a simp lemma whose left side is `(piEquivOfFG I M hI).toLinearMap`. `piEquivOfFG_apply` already covers the pointwise form, and `piEquivOfFG_apply_apply` covers the coordinate form. All three duplicate the same fact (`piEquivOfFG` is `pi I M`) at different levels of application, with no simp lemma for the coercion `⇑(piEquivOfFG I M hI)`. For function-level statements such as `⇑(piEquivOfFG I M hI) = ⇑(pi I M)`, one of these forms will match depending on how the term is elaborated.
findings.proposed_change: State the canonical simp lemma once, as the coercion lemma `⇑(piEquivOfFG I M hI) = ⇑(pi I M)`. This also covers function-level uses. Keep `toLinearMap` as a plain, non-simp lemma, or derive it with `LinearMap.ext`. Keep the pointwise form only if it is the chosen normal form.
findings.benefit: A single simp lemma for the equivalence-to-`pi` rewrite replaces three overlapping ones. This makes simp behaviour on `piEquivOfFG` more predictable.
